edges.description: The fusion is what drives the cluster's expression.

Putting the microRNAs into cells raises DNMT3B and lowers RBL2 together. The authors read the DNMT3B rise as mediated by RBL2, a known repressor of DNMT3B, and hedge that reading; the edge is recorded at their strength.
The amplified cluster is one arm of a self-reinforcing circuit.
The authors read the methylation landscape as mediated by this isoform. Their own wording is that the data suggest it, and the edge is recorded at that strength.
LIN28A within the circuit holds let-7 down: removing LIN28 raises let-7. By what step is not stated by any cached source.

The raised IGF/PI3K/mTOR axis is the entry's proposed route from the microRNA defect to a proliferative, undifferentiated population. No cached source links that axis to a progenitor population, so the step is the entry's reading rather than a reported result.

edges.description: Loss of DICER1 function impairs microRNA processing. The convergence on let-7 specifically is inferred from DICER1's general role in producing mature microRNAs, not demonstrated in this disease by any source cited here.
Loss of DICER1 function induces the R-loop-associated instability, which is how this arm reaches the structural-variant burden the C19MC arm reaches by another route.
The entrapped population is what the tumour is built from.

nodes.description: Preclinical only: the bromodomain inhibitor JQ1 abrogates the circuit and ETMR cells die. The cited sentence names no experimental system, so the entry does not say which one it was, and no clinical use is recorded in any cached source.

evidence.reference_title: A C19MC-LIN28A-MYCN Oncogenic Circuit Driven by Hijacked Super-enhancers Is a Distinct Therapeutic Vulnerability in ETMRs: A Lethal Brain Tumor.
evidence.snippet: Our data show that this powerful oncogenic circuit, which entraps an early neural lineage network, is potently abrogated by bromodomain inhibitor JQ1, leading to ETMR cell death.

nodes.description: A focal structural rearrangement amplifies the C19MC microRNA cluster at 19q13.42 and fuses it to TTYH1, and the fusion is what drives the cluster's expression. The cluster's normal expression is restricted to undifferentiated and germinal tissues and falls as embryonic stem cells differentiate, so the lesion puts it at high level where it is normally low.

evidence.reference_title: Fusion of TTYH1 with the C19MC microRNA cluster drives expression of a brain-specific DNMT3B isoform in the embryonal brain tumor ETMR.
evidence.snippet: We performed integrated genetic and epigenetic analyses of 12 ETMR samples and identified, in all cases, C19MC fusions to TTYH1 driving expression of the microRNAs.

evidence.reference_title: Focal genomic amplification at 19q13.42 comprises a powerful diagnostic marker for embryonal tumors with ependymoblastic rosettes.

nodes.description: A self-reinforcing circuit joining the amplified microRNA cluster, the pluripotency factor LIN28A and MYCN, held together by an MYCN core transcriptional network and by super-enhancers created both by long-range MYCN DNA interactions and by the C19MC fusions themselves. Its effect on the cell is to entrap an early neural lineage network.

evidence.snippet: Here we investigated C19MC oncogenic mechanisms and discovered a C19MC-LIN28A-MYCN circuit fueled by multiple complex regulatory loops including an MYCN core transcriptional network and super-enhancers resulting from long-range MYCN DNA interactions and C19MC gene fusions.

nodes.description: The alternative driver arm. Tumours without C19MC amplification frequently carry germline DICER1 mutations, and biallelic DICER1 mutation is reported in infratentorially located C19MC-negative tumours, at about 5% of all ETMR. How this arm reaches the microRNA defect is not demonstrated by any source cached here: the allele classes, the order of the two hits, and the convergence on let-7 specifically are all absent from them.

evidence.reference_title: The molecular landscape of ETMR at diagnosis and relapse.
evidence.snippet: We found that patients with tumours in which the proposed driver C19MC2-4 was not amplified frequently had germline mutations in DICER1 or other microRNA-related aberrations such as somatic amplification of miR-17-92 (also known as MIR17HG).

nodes.description: A DNA methylation pattern distinct from other tumours and from normal tissue, found in ETMR tumours, cell lines and xenografts alike. It is a consequence of the mechanism rather than a step in it, and a methylation classifier is what assigns the entity in practice.

nodes.description: The tumour itself: a rare and aggressive embryonal CNS neoplasm of early childhood, defined by its multilayered rosettes and by the C19MC lesion.

evidence.snippet: Embryonal tumors with multilayered rosettes (ETMRs) are rare, highly aggressive pediatric brain neoplasms characterized by early onset and dismal prognosis.

nodes.description: Extreme overexpression of a DNMT3B isoform transcribed from an alternative promoter that is normally active only during the first weeks of neural tube development. This is the step that makes the disease epigenetic as much as genetic: the methyltransferase itself is a developmental isoform running far outside its window.

evidence.reference_title: Fusion of TTYH1 with the C19MC microRNA cluster drives expression of a brain-specific DNMT3B isoform in the embryonal brain tumor ETMR.
evidence.snippet: We detected extreme overexpression of a previously uncharacterized isoform of DNMT3B originating at an alternative promoter that is active only in the first weeks of neural tube development.

nodes.description: The oncogenic circuit entraps an early neural lineage network, and blocking the circuit kills the cells. What the entrapped population is, and how it relates to the entity's multilayered rosettes, is not established by any source cached here. The cell type and process bound below are the most specific the sources reach - a nestin-positive line, and proliferation as a general property of the cluster's microRNAs - not an identification of that population.

evidence.snippet: Finally, we show that targeting R-loops with topoisomerase and PARP inhibitors might be an effective treatment strategy for this deadly disease.

nodes.description: Low mature let-7 alongside high LIN28, with the IGF/PI3K/mTOR axis raised. Removing LIN28 raises let-7 and lowers that axis. The authors read this as consistent with a functional Lin28/let-7 axis in ETMR, and that is the strength recorded here: no cached source manipulates let-7 itself, so let-7 is not shown to be the intermediate, and the same paper notes that LIN28 proteins act on many transcripts besides let-7.
